summary.oneLiner: Cantabil Retail India Limited is an integrated Indian fashion retailer that designs, manufactures, brands and retails ready-to-wear apparel and accessories for the whole family under a mid-premium value positioning.
summary.business: Cantabil is a pan-India apparel company with an integrated business model spanning design, manufacturing, branding and retailing of formal, casual, party and ultra-casual ready-to-wear garments and accessories for men, women and kids. It sells primarily through a network of 652 Exclusive Brand Outlets (EBOs) across 308 cities and 21 states/UTs, plus online marketplaces and its own e-commerce channel, targeting middle- and upper-middle-income consumers.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated model across design, manufacturing, branding and retailing gives control over quality, cost and speed to shelf|High company-operated store mix (~81% of network) provides closer control over merchandise, presentation, staffing and local execution versus franchise-heavy peers|Family-wear brand positioning ('One Brand. Every Family') allows cross-selling women's, kids' and accessories to an existing men's-wear customer base|Debt-light balance sheet funded by internal accruals — no conventional external borrowings apart from store lease liabilities — giving flexibility to invest, relocate or exit underperforming stores|Disciplined store portfolio optimization: proactively phasing out underperforming stores in favour of modernized, larger-format stores in stronger catchments|Family-store format delivers EBITDA margins about 1.5 percentage points above men-only-format stores due to shared lease and team supporting a wider basket
currentContext.strategies: Vision 2027: reach ₹1,000 crore revenue, 725 stores across 330 cities, and 8-10% online contribution, guided by five pillars connecting market opportunity with business capability|Pillar 1 - Retail, Product and Customer Focus: match store format, assortment and service to each catchment; improve adjacent-category (women's wear, kids' wear, accessories) productivity within the existing family-store base|Pillar 2 - Manufacturing, Sourcing and Inventory Management: retain owned manufacturing for technically-demanding garments while flexing capacity via job-work and sourcing; improve forecasting, replenishment and ageing action to turn inventory faster|Pillar 3 - Technology and Digital: complete the D365 ERP rollout for a connected view across stores, warehouses, production and finance; evaluate AI retail tools for footfall, conversion and compliance subject to business case; grow online on profitable terms|Pillar 4 - Brand and Marketing: rely on the store as the principal brand medium, supported by measured, ROI-tracked marketing spend of around 1.5% of revenue|Pillar 5 - People Centricity: stated as one of the five growth pillars (no further detail in this bundle)|Protect the economics of growth: fund expansion primarily through operating cash flow while growing digital access on profitable terms and strengthening people capability|Improve the quality of the retail estate: select catchments carefully, enlarge proven locations where economics support it, and correct weaker investments before they absorb disproportionate capital and attention|Turn stock and information faster: improve forecasting, replenishment, transfers and ageing action while completing the connected information view across stores, warehouses, product, manufacturing and finance|The Company follows a formal, Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (filed as an annexure to the Directors' Report) that sets out the parameters and circumstances the Board considers when determining shareholder distributions. In practice it pays both an interim dividend, declared by the Board mid-year, and a final dividend, recommended at year-end and subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. The Company confirmed it has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company during the reporting period.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26 Cantabil grew its store network by a net 52-53 outlets to roughly 652-653 Exclusive Brand Outlets across 308 cities and 21 states, with total retail area expanding 13.8% to 9.15 lakh sq. ft. Family-format stores were the principal expansion vehicle, rising from 210 to 238, alongside growth in men's stores (335 to 351) and women-and-kids stores (54 to 63). North and West India remain the core markets, with Central and East India cited as the measured route for geographic diversification. During the year the Company moved into a new corporate office, expanded warehousing capacity and continued investment in its own manufacturing facility to support the wider store network and product range. It is also implementing an end-to-end ERP solution connecting stores, product, purchasing, manufacturing, warehouses, inventory and finance, intended to enable earlier replenishment, stock transfers, ageing action and production decisions. Store-count growth is being paired with an active store-portfolio-optimization and store-modernization programme that phases out underperforming stores in favour of larger, modernized formats in stronger catchments.
currentContext.mdna: India's medium-term consumption outlook draws strength from rising household incomes, urbanisation, a growing middle-income population and wider physical/digital access, expanding demand beyond the largest cities and increasing preference for organised retail, branded products and dependable value|Projected real GDP growth of 6.8-7.2% in FY2026-27, with easing inflation and policy continuity, provides a supportive setting for discretionary consumption, though demand may remain sensitive to food inflation, employment conditions and global volatility|Affluent and aspirational households are expected to account for nearly 55% of India's incremental consumption growth, fuelling demand for branded and premium apparel; Generation Z is emerging as a powerful consumption cohort favouring digital-first, trend-led, personalised brand experiences|Tier II, III and IV cities are becoming more important as consumers there seek current designs, reliable quality and a consistent shopping experience within a considered budget, underpinning the Company's network-expansion strategy|Omnichannel convergence and D2C models are reshaping consumer engagement; management positions online growth as an access-and-learning channel that must remain profitable after commissions, discounts, fulfilment and returns rather than a scale-at-any-cost play|Volatility in cotton, fabric, energy and logistics costs and shorter fashion cycles require closer industry-wide control over product planning, sourcing, inventory and markdowns|Manufacturing, logistics and energy costs in India remain 15-20% higher than competing markets such as Bangladesh and Vietnam, an industry-level cost-competitiveness headwind

risks.note: A slowdown in the broader economy could impact overall business operations and expansion timelines, since discretionary apparel spending is sensitive to macro conditions.

The Company operates in a highly competitive apparel retail market with numerous organised and unorganised players; increased competition and aggressive pricing by new entrants could impact total sales and compress profit margins.

Volatility in raw material prices (e.g. cotton, fabric), energy costs and other input expenses can impact the Company's cost structure and profitability; management monitors commodity and energy markets to manage timing of procurement.
Failing to uphold high-quality standards could harm the Company's reputation and affect future opportunities, given that brand recall is central to Cantabil's value proposition.

Availability of funds and prudent placement of surplus funds is important to operations; the Company invests with counterparties assessed for creditworthiness, though retail collections themselves carry limited risk as sales are largely cash/digital.

The value of the new end-to-end ERP platform connecting stores, purchasing, manufacturing, warehouses, inventory and finance depends on phased implementation, process discipline and user adoption — a rollout that is not yet complete.

Turnover is concentrated in a single business activity (retail sale of apparel, ~98% of turnover per BRSR disclosure) and the Company has no international operations, leaving it exposed to conditions specific to the Indian apparel retail market.

thesis (one line): Debt-free, vertically-integrated value-apparel retailer compounding via disciplined EBO rollout (bigger family stores), best-in-class ~60% gross margin and tight opex — targeting INR1,000 cr revenue / 725 stores in FY27 with steady 5-6% SSSG.

| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 | FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue from ops | INR253.5 cr | INR219.8 cr | +15% | INR852.6 cr | INR721.1 cr* | +18% | *FY25 base (transcript typo'd "FY21") |
| EBITDA | INR78.1 cr | INR58.4 cr | +34% | INR264.3 cr | INR204.8 cr | +29% | Post-Ind-AS 116 (lease added back) |
| EBITDA margin | 30.8% | 26.6% | +420 bps | 31.0% | 28.4% | +260 bps | Highest-ever EBITDA |
| PAT | INR29.2 cr | INR22.5 cr | +30% | INR95.8 cr | INR74.9 cr | +28% | Highest annual profit |
| PAT margin | 11.5% | 10.2% | +130 bps | 11.2% | 10.4% | +80 bps | Reported; no separate norm. given |
| Gross margin | ~57% (Q4) | ~53-54% | +350-400 bps | 60.4% | ~58% (FY25) | — | FY24 was 56.2% |
| SSSG | — | — | — | ~5% | — | — | April'26 also ~5% |
| Store count | 652 stores | — | — | 652 | — | — | Gross 91 opened, 38 churned (renewals/closures) |
| Retail area | 9.15 lakh sq ft | — | — | 9.15 lk sf | ~8.05 lk sf | +~1.1 lk sf | Avg new store ~1,700 sq ft |
| Net debt | Debt-free | — | — | Debt-free | — | — | INR~50 cr cash surplus |

**One-offs / non-recurring:** New corporate office + online warehouse (~INR50-55 cr ex-land) capitalised in FY26, depreciation now flowing; lease saving of ~INR1.5-2 cr/yr from vacating old office to start Q2/Q3 FY27. INR25 cr intercorporate loan to non-related party at ~12% (vs market 6-7%), one-year, may be unwound in FY27.
guidance (critical):
| Guide item | FY27 guidance |
|---|---|
| **Revenue** | INR1,000 cr target (~+17% over INR852.6 cr) |
| **SSSG** | Minimum 5-6% maintained; could reach 7-8% (early to call) |
| **Store count** | 725 stores target; gross ~90-100 adds; net ~70-75% of gross (i.e. ~70 net) |
| **Retail area** | +15-20% (min 15%) per annum |
| **Gross margin** | Maintain ~60% (internal guidance; ±1%) |
| **EBITDA margin** | ~30% sustainable (anchored to 60% GM) |
| **Lease rent (Ind-AS)** | ~INR100 cr FY26 → ~INR108-110 cr FY27; actual rental ~INR99 cr FY26 |
| **Capex** | ~INR1,800 per sq ft for ~90-100 new stores; ~INR100 cr range; expect per-sq-ft capex to FALL (new lower-cost furniture/fixture design) |
| **Footwear** | ~2% of sales FY26 (INR14 cr, +40% YoY) → target 3-4%; growth via online |
| **Kids wear** | ~2-3% of sales → ~4-4.5% next year |
| **Marketing spend** | ~1.7% → up to ~1.8-2.0% |
pipeline (store rollout):
- FY26: gross 91 stores opened; net base 652 (38 stores churned — ~24-25 renewals/relocations on 9-yr lease expiry, ~13 performance-based closures).
- ~45 stores in active pipeline at call time; ~10% of base (~65 stores) comes up for renewal annually.
- FY27: 725-store target; new stores larger (~1,700 sq ft avg vs 1,100 three years ago, 1,400 FY26 avg).
- Breakeven ~6 months; full maturity ~1.5-2 years (same for men's vs family stores).
segment (own vs franchise; geographies):
- **COCO ~80% / Franchise ~20%.** Big/high-rental prime stores stay COCO (franchisees shy from high investment); Tier-3 / lower-rental markets take franchise.
- **Format mix:** ~45% of stores are family stores (carry kids wear + women's); rest men's-led.
- **Geography:** Pan-India; larger-format constrained in Maharashtra/Gujarat (big properties scarce). Nepal: ~3-4 stores (multi-brand + EBO mix), selling/distribution model, ~1.5% of business, lower transfer-pricing margin.
- **Online:** Q4 e-comm ~INR11 cr (FY25 ~INR9.88 cr, +~10% value / +~13% volume); Myntra + Flipkart ~65-70% of online.
growth / optionality:
- Core driver: store expansion to 725 + bigger family-store format (higher EBITDA, ~+1.5% vs men's stores).
- Online footwear & kids-wear penetration ramp (footwear to 3-4%, kids to 4.5%).
- New automated (WMS) online warehouse — 4 floors of new 11-storey HQ dedicated to e-comm fulfilment.
- Manufacturing integration: ~60% own/controlled (factory ~25% + job-work ~35%), 40% accessories outsourced; specialised suit/blazer plant at Bahadurgarh (18-20 lakh garment capacity) gives margin edge; capacity expansion of suit unit possible as demand rises — but company explicitly stays "core retailer," prefers job-work over new own plants.
- Export/Nepal master-franchise & overseas JV optionality — low priority vs INR1,000 cr India runway.
- Fast fashion explicitly NOT pursued — positioned as basics (UNIQLO-like, not Zara).
margins & cost:
- GM expanded 56.2% (FY24) → ~58% (FY25) → 60.4% (FY26); Q4 GM ~57% lifted by product-mix, pricing correction, slight GST help.
- Retail (front-end) cost 34% → 33% of sales on operating leverage; back-end corporate cost ~8%, controlled. Expect to hold ±1%.
- Gross margin held at ~60% even with some raw-material inflation (cost shared customer/company).
- Avg bill value rising ~10% p.a. (inflation + better product mix).
capex (store + manufacturing):
- ~INR1,800/sq ft per new store; ~INR100 cr annual capex from internal accrual; per-sq-ft capex to decline on new cheaper fixture design.
- New corporate office + online warehouse capitalised FY26 (~INR50-55 cr ex-land).
- ~INR10 cr CWIP: extra floor at Bahadurgarh factory (~50%), HQ finishing (C-12), ~INR1.5 cr for stores opening Q1 FY27.
- Heavier capex/expansion phase signalled from Q3 FY27.
capital allocation:
- Debt-free; FY26 cash surplus ~INR50 cr — half deployed as INR25 cr intercorporate loan (non-related party) at ~12% for 1 yr (vs 6-7% market), likely unwound in FY27.
- No dividend/buyback discussed explicitly; surplus earmarked for store expansion + better-return deployment from Q3 FY27.
- Healthy balance sheet positioned for continued growth investment.
risks:
- **Demand:** Discretionary apparel sensitive to inflation / monetary tightening; analyst flagged SSSG correlation to monetary policy — mgmt counters with marketing + incentive levers (April'26 SSSG held ~5%).
- **Inventory:** Aging risk; provisioning 0% (<1 yr), 10% (1-3 yr), 50% (>3 yr); ~70-75% of inventory within 1.5 yrs; inventory days 109-110 (down from ~123), working capital ~105 days (down from ~115); guardrail "not beyond 120 days."
- **Execution:** Larger-store format + renewal churn (10%/yr); new-market adaptability (mgmt says response good).
- **Raw material / input cost** inflation pressuring margins.
mgmt tone: Confident, consistent, granular on operations. Repeatedly anchors to 60% GM / 30% EBITDA / 5-6% SSSG as "promised and delivered." Emphasises "tight negotiator," debt-free, disciplined cash use. Comfortable defending margin/SSSG durability through inflation; measured on optionality (Nepal/export/manufacturing) — keeps focus on India retail runway. 5-yr revenue CAGR ~22%, PAT CAGR ~26%. "Vision 2027."
non-obvious takeaways:
- Bigger family stores carry ~+1.5% EBITDA margin over men's stores — structural driver of margin lift as format mix shifts.
- ~10% of base churns annually on 9-yr lease expiry → reported gross adds (91) far exceed net adds; "net 70-75% of gross."
- Rent/sq ft FELL to INR115 (FY25 INR120) — negotiating power despite expansion; total actual rent ~INR99 cr.
- Online billing-pattern change at Myntra/Flipkart distorts value growth (volume +13% vs value +10%).
- Suit/blazer is the genuinely specialised, hard-to-replicate (imported machinery) in-house piece; rest deliberately job-worked — they choose to stay asset-light retailer, not manufacturer.
- New HQ online warehouse fully WMS-automated — supports online scale-up ambition.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ / ⭐ — None material flagged for external beneficiaries.
- Input-cost inflation is the recurring challenge; mitigation is internal (mix, pricing, lower-cost fixtures, job-work flexibility) rather than creating identifiable third-party beneficiaries.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

themes.title: Branded innerwear & domestic apparel
themes.need: Branded innerwear and domestic apparel are driven by rural recovery, GST 2.0 and distribution reach - a domestic-consumption thesis, not the China+1/FTA export tailwind powering exporters and synthetics.
themes.driver: Rural recovery + GST 2.0 demand pull and distribution-led volume growth.

hero.oneLiner: Cantabil Retail India Limited is an integrated Indian fashion retailer that designs, manufactures, brands and retails ready-to-wear apparel and accessories for the whole family under a mid-premium value positioning.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Cantabil Retail India Limited is an integrated Indian fashion retailer that designs, manufactures, brands and retails ready-to-wear apparel and accessories for the whole family under a mid-premium value positioning.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cantabil is a pan-India apparel company with an integrated business model spanning design, manufacturing, branding and retailing of formal, casual, party and ultra-casual ready-to-wear garments and accessories for men, women and kids. It sells primarily through a network of 652 Exclusive Brand Outlets (EBOs) across 308 cities and 21 states/UTs, plus online marketplaces and its own e-commerce channel, targeting middle- and upper-middle-income consumers.

segment_detail.title: Segment (own vs franchise; geographies)
segment_detail.body:
- **COCO ~80% / Franchise ~20%.** Big/high-rental prime stores stay COCO (franchisees shy from high investment); Tier-3 / lower-rental markets take franchise.
- **Format mix:** ~45% of stores are family stores (carry kids wear + women's); rest men's-led.
- **Geography:** Pan-India; larger-format constrained in Maharashtra/Gujarat (big properties scarce). Nepal: ~3-4 stores (multi-brand + EBO mix), selling/distribution model, ~1.5% of business, lower transfer-pricing margin.
- **Online:** Q4 e-comm ~INR11 cr (FY25 ~INR9.88 cr, +~10% value / +~13% volume); Myntra + Flipkart ~65-70% of online.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Men's Wear:** Formal wear, Casual wear, Party wear, Ultra-casual wear
- **Women's Wear:** Formal wear, Casual wear, Party wear, Ultra-casual wear
- **Kids' Wear:** Kids apparel
- **Accessories:** Men's accessories

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Pan-India retail across 308 cities and 21 states/UTs
- Middle- and upper-middle-income consumer segments
- Tier II, III and IV cities (growing share of expansion)
- Online marketplaces and own e-commerce (~6% of revenue)
- Exports (negligible, 0.17% of turnover)

order_book.title: Pipeline (store rollout)
order_book.body:
- FY26: gross 91 stores opened; net base 652 (38 stores churned — ~24-25 renewals/relocations on 9-yr lease expiry, ~13 performance-based closures).
- ~45 stores in active pipeline at call time; ~10% of base (~65 stores) comes up for renewal annually.
- FY27: 725-store target; new stores larger (~1,700 sq ft avg vs 1,100 three years ago, 1,400 FY26 avg).
- Breakeven ~6 months; full maturity ~1.5-2 years (same for men's vs family stores).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
| Guide item | FY27 guidance |
|---|---|
| **Revenue** | INR1,000 cr target (~+17% over INR852.6 cr) |
| **SSSG** | Minimum 5-6% maintained; could reach 7-8% (early to call) |
| **Store count** | 725 stores target; gross ~90-100 adds; net ~70-75% of gross (i.e. ~70 net) |
| **Retail area** | +15-20% (min 15%) per annum |
| **Gross margin** | Maintain ~60% (internal guidance; ±1%) |
| **EBITDA margin** | ~30% sustainable (anchored to 60% GM) |
| **Lease rent (Ind-AS)** | ~INR100 cr FY26 → ~INR108-110 cr FY27; actual rental ~INR99 cr FY26 |
| **Capex** | ~INR1,800 per sq ft for ~90-100 new stores; ~INR100 cr range; expect per-sq-ft capex to FALL (new lower-cost furniture/fixture design) |
| **Footwear** | ~2% of sales FY26 (INR14 cr, +40% YoY) → target 3-4%; growth via online |
| **Kids wear** | ~2-3% of sales → ~4-4.5% next year |
| **Marketing spend** | ~1.7% → up to ~1.8-2.0% |

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Core driver: store expansion to 725 + bigger family-store format (higher EBITDA, ~+1.5% vs men's stores).
- Online footwear & kids-wear penetration ramp (footwear to 3-4%, kids to 4.5%).
- New automated (WMS) online warehouse — 4 floors of new 11-storey HQ dedicated to e-comm fulfilment.
- Manufacturing integration: ~60% own/controlled (factory ~25% + job-work ~35%), 40% accessories outsourced; specialised suit/blazer plant at Bahadurgarh (18-20 lakh garment capacity) gives margin edge; capacity expansion of suit unit possible as demand rises — but company explicitly stays "core retailer," prefers job-work over new own plants.
- Export/Nepal master-franchise & overseas JV optionality — low priority vs INR1,000 cr India runway.
- Fast fashion explicitly NOT pursued — positioned as basics (UNIQLO-like, not Zara).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's medium-term consumption outlook draws strength from rising household incomes, urbanisation, a growing middle-income population and wider physical/digital access, expanding demand beyond the largest cities and increasing preference for organised retail, branded products and dependable value
- Projected real GDP growth of 6.8-7.2% in FY2026-27, with easing inflation and policy continuity, provides a supportive setting for discretionary consumption, though demand may remain sensitive to food inflation, employment conditions and global volatility
- Affluent and aspirational households are expected to account for nearly 55% of India's incremental consumption growth, fuelling demand for branded and premium apparel; Generation Z is emerging as a powerful consumption cohort favouring digital-first, trend-led, personalised brand experiences
- Tier II, III and IV cities are becoming more important as consumers there seek current designs, reliable quality and a consistent shopping experience within a considered budget, underpinning the Company's network-expansion strategy
- Omnichannel convergence and D2C models are reshaping consumer engagement; management positions online growth as an access-and-learning channel that must remain profitable after commissions, discounts, fulfilment and returns rather than a scale-at-any-cost play
- Volatility in cotton, fabric, energy and logistics costs and shorter fashion cycles require closer industry-wide control over product planning, sourcing, inventory and markdowns
- Manufacturing, logistics and energy costs in India remain 15-20% higher than competing markets such as Bangladesh and Vietnam, an industry-level cost-competitiveness headwind

margins.title: Margins & cost
margins.body:
- GM expanded 56.2% (FY24) → ~58% (FY25) → 60.4% (FY26); Q4 GM ~57% lifted by product-mix, pricing correction, slight GST help.
- Retail (front-end) cost 34% → 33% of sales on operating leverage; back-end corporate cost ~8%, controlled. Expect to hold ±1%.
- Gross margin held at ~60% even with some raw-material inflation (cost shared customer/company).
- Avg bill value rising ~10% p.a. (inflation + better product mix).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Debt-free; FY26 cash surplus ~INR50 cr — half deployed as INR25 cr intercorporate loan (non-related party) at ~12% for 1 yr (vs 6-7% market), likely unwound in FY27.
- No dividend/buyback discussed explicitly; surplus earmarked for store expansion + better-return deployment from Q3 FY27.
- Healthy balance sheet positioned for continued growth investment.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY2025-26 Cantabil grew its store network by a net 52-53 outlets to roughly 652-653 Exclusive Brand Outlets across 308 cities and 21 states, with total retail area expanding 13.8% to 9.15 lakh sq. ft. Family-format stores were the principal expansion vehicle, rising from 210 to 238, alongside growth in men's stores (335 to 351) and women-and-kids stores (54 to 63). North and West India remain the core markets, with Central and East India cited as the measured route for geographic diversification. During the year the Company moved into a new corporate office, expanded warehousing capacity and continued investment in its own manufacturing facility to support the wider store network and product range. It is also implementing an end-to-end ERP solution connecting stores, product, purchasing, manufacturing, warehouses, inventory and finance, intended to enable earlier replenishment, stock transfers, ageing action and production decisions. Store-count growth is being paired with an active store-portfolio-optimization and store-modernization programme that phases out underperforming stores in favour of larger, modernized formats in stronger catchments.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident, consistent, granular on operations. Repeatedly anchors to 60% GM / 30% EBITDA / 5-6% SSSG as "promised and delivered." Emphasises "tight negotiator," debt-free, disciplined cash use. Comfortable defending margin/SSSG durability through inflation; measured on optionality (Nepal/export/manufacturing) — keeps focus on India retail runway. 5-yr revenue CAGR ~22%, PAT CAGR ~26%. "Vision 2027."

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated model across design, manufacturing, branding and retailing gives control over quality, cost and speed to shelf
- High company-operated store mix (~81% of network) provides closer control over merchandise, presentation, staffing and local execution versus franchise-heavy peers
- Family-wear brand positioning ('One Brand. Every Family') allows cross-selling women's, kids' and accessories to an existing men's-wear customer base
- Debt-light balance sheet funded by internal accruals — no conventional external borrowings apart from store lease liabilities — giving flexibility to invest, relocate or exit underperforming stores
- Disciplined store portfolio optimization: proactively phasing out underperforming stores in favour of modernized, larger-format stores in stronger catchments
- Family-store format delivers EBITDA margins about 1.5 percentage points above men-only-format stores due to shared lease and team supporting a wider basket

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Demand:** Discretionary apparel sensitive to inflation / monetary tightening; analyst flagged SSSG correlation to monetary policy — mgmt counters with marketing + incentive levers (April'26 SSSG held ~5%).
- **Inventory:** Aging risk; provisioning 0% (<1 yr), 10% (1-3 yr), 50% (>3 yr); ~70-75% of inventory within 1.5 yrs; inventory days 109-110 (down from ~123), working capital ~105 days (down from ~115); guardrail "not beyond 120 days."
- **Execution:** Larger-store format + renewal churn (10%/yr); new-market adaptability (mgmt says response good).
- **Raw material / input cost** inflation pressuring margins.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Bigger family stores carry ~+1.5% EBITDA margin over men's stores — structural driver of margin lift as format mix shifts.
- ~10% of base churns annually on 9-yr lease expiry → reported gross adds (91) far exceed net adds; "net 70-75% of gross."
- Rent/sq ft FELL to INR115 (FY25 INR120) — negotiating power despite expansion; total actual rent ~INR99 cr.
- Online billing-pattern change at Myntra/Flipkart distorts value growth (volume +13% vs value +10%).
- Suit/blazer is the genuinely specialised, hard-to-replicate (imported machinery) in-house piece; rest deliberately job-worked — they choose to stay asset-light retailer, not manufacturer.
- New HQ online warehouse fully WMS-automated — supports online scale-up ambition.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Vision 2027: reach ₹1,000 crore revenue, 725 stores across 330 cities, and 8-10% online contribution, guided by five pillars connecting market opportunity with business capability
- Pillar 1 - Retail, Product and Customer Focus: match store format, assortment and service to each catchment; improve adjacent-category (women's wear, kids' wear, accessories) productivity within the existing family-store base
- Pillar 2 - Manufacturing, Sourcing and Inventory Management: retain owned manufacturing for technically-demanding garments while flexing capacity via job-work and sourcing; improve forecasting, …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ✅ / ⭐ — None material flagged for external beneficiaries.
- Input-cost inflation is the recurring challenge; mitigation is internal (mix, pricing, lower-cost fixtures, job-work flexibility) rather than creating identifiable third-party beneficiaries.

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Rev INR253.5 cr (+15% YoY); EBITDA INR78.1 cr (+34%, margin 30.8%); PAT INR29.2 cr (+30%, margin 11.5%); 652 stores / 9.15 lk sq ft. FY26: Rev INR852.6 cr (+18%), EBITDA INR264.3 cr (margin 31%), PAT INR95.8 cr (margin 11.2%), GM 60.4%, SSSG ~5%, debt-free, ~INR50 cr cash surplus. Guidance FY27: INR1,000 cr rev / 725 stores / 5-6%+ SSSG / 60% GM / 30% EBITDA. New HQ + online warehouse capitalised. INR25 cr intercorporate loan @12%.
- (Prior quarters not in this source; reference: GM trajectory FY24 56.2% → FY26 60.4%; avg store size 1,100 → 1,400 → new 1,700 sq ft.)

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Dual reporting] The deck presents every P&L twice - on Ind AS 116 and "PRE IND AS 116" basis - producing two different margin sets for the same period (e.g. FY26 EBITDA 264.3 / 31.0% margin under Ind AS vs 162.1 / 19.0% pre-Ind AS).
- [Marketplace disruption] "During FY26, Myntra changed the billing system, impacting absolute revenue growth numbers."
- [Governance] Promoter-led board - Deepak Bansal (Chairman & MD) "Founded, Promoted and launched Brand 'Cantabil' in 2000", with Vijay Bansal as Whole Time Director; three independent directors (Lalit Kumar, Rajeev Sharma, Arpana Jain).
- [Deck defect] On the independent-directors slide the biography under the heading "LALIT KUMAR" describes "Mr Rajeev Sharma" (Haryana Civil Services 1976, IAS 1989 batch), so the name-to-profile binding on that slide is unreliable.
- [IR] Investor relations handled by Marathon Capital Advisory Pvt. Ltd; company contact is Mr. Shivendra Nigam (CFO).
